subject: Hosted API latency & TPS: sudden p95/p99 spikes and tokens/sec sag
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@apexcommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API: sudden p95/p99 spikes and TPS drop

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp degradation this morning on our Hosted API integration (prod region us-west-2). Two observable problems: p95/p99 response times jumped (~600ms -> ~2.1s p95, ~1.2s -> ~5.3s p99) and the tokens-per-second throughput for our long-turn requests dropped from ~1,050–1,250 tps historically to ~320–400 tps. Error rate (5xx) is ~2.1% over last 45 minutes.

Attached is a small sample of request ids and timing (apex_sample_requests.log) and a short CSV with our per-node token/sec snapshot. Impact: our streaming-first features are timing out for several customers. This started ~2028-05-22T08:40:00Z.

Can you confirm whether any changes rolled overnight? We need a high-priority investigation and, if needed, a mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Samir
VP Engineering, Apex Commerce

Attachments: apex_sample_requests.log

Plan: Karthik will lead triage; we will confirm whether any quantization or kernel selection changes landed on the hosted fleet overnight and propose a targeted rollback / canary. I'll keep you updated every 30–45 minutes until we have a mitigation.

—Marissa

Attachments: apex_sample_requests.log (referenced)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-22T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: sudden p95/p99 spikes and TPS drop

Marissa / Laura — summary from the initial triage:

What we observed:
- Replayed Samir's requests in our staging harness; reproduction is consistent with their metrics: tokens/sec drops by ~70% on longer sequences (>=1024 tokens).
- The timing aligns with a deployment in our hosted fleet at 2028-05-22T02:12:00Z that included a quantization profile tweak and a kernel-selection override (deploy tag: q2-quant-1).
- The kernel selector change added a new hint that prefers int4-friendly kernels and updates the fallback order; we suspect a regression where the runtime chooses a suboptimal kernel path for certain attention shapes, increasing per-token latency and blocking KV-cache batching optimizations.

Immediate action items:
1) Roll back the kernel-selector override in the hosted fleet (patch ready).
2) Spin an isolated canary with the previous kernel-selection policy and run the exact Apex request set.
3) Collect perf counters (kernel hit/miss, batch sizes, kv-cache hit-rate) during canary.

I've attached the diff that reverts the selector change (kernel-selector-diff.patch). If canary looks good, we will stage a fleet-wide incremental rollback with a staged ramp over 30m.

Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kernel-selector-diff.patch
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-05-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: sudden p95/p99 spikes and TPS drop

Samir — update from the engineering side: Karthik found a likely culprit (kernel selector change tied to the q2-quant-1 rollout). We intend to run a canary rollback tonight at 2028-05-23T02:00:00Z UTC for a single region (us-west-2), replay your batch, and measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec.

Would Apex be available for a brief window during that canary to validate from your side? If you'd prefer we can do a staged rollback without customer validation, but we'd like an explicit OK before affecting production routing.

For transparency, here's our mutual-action-plan tracker: https://docs.redwood.com/mutual-action-plans/APX-7832

We will also capture a post-mortem and share the perf counters and the kernel hit/miss stats.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Hosted API: sudden p95/p99 spikes and TPS drop — leadership sync

Looping leadership for the SLA / credits conversation and to brief on next steps.

Summary for execs:
- Impact: Apex Commerce reported p95/p99 regressions and ~65–75% tokens-per-second drop for long sequences; customer-facing.
- Root cause (current hypothesis): a kernel-selection heuristic introduced with deploy tag q2-quant-1 caused the runtime to prefer an int4-optimized kernel path that is suboptimal for several attention shapes; this both increased per-token CPU/GPU scheduling overhead and prevented effective KV-cache batching.
- Mitigation taken: we performed a staged canary rollback overnight (2028-05-23T02:00:00Z UTC), validated with Apex request replays; metrics returned to baseline (p95/p99 and tokens/sec). Fleet rollback completed 2028-05-23T04:10:00Z UTC with monitored ramp.
- Next actions: full post-mortem (target: 72h), identify additional guardrails for kernel-selection rollouts (feature flags, darker-launch telemetry), evaluate opt-in per-customer kernel policies, prepare an SLA remediation proposal for Apex.

Requesting: Rishi / Marissa to lead customer remediation conversation and determine credit amount; Karthik / infra to provide the perf counters, decision logs, and the complete rollback diff for inclusion in the post-mortem.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
